## Findings
- claim-1: The supplied source-29 full-text block is ar5iv content and truncates equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1, so their complete verbatim text is unavailable here. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 149-188]
- claim-2: Theorem 4.4 applies to every valid \(\varphi\); its cases \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) and \(N>\min(j,n-r-i)\) are proof branches, not additional theorem hypotheses. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-494]
- claim-3: Theorem 4.5 derives the absence of its specified syzygy from Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 495-502]
- claim-4: No supplied non-ar5iv full-text provider for source-29 contains the requested uncorrupted bounded excerpt; hence the complete valid-tuple inequalities cannot be transcribed or classified as theorem hypotheses.
- claim-5: The requested source certificate is **not established**.
## Strategy
Compared the supplied source-29 record with the persisted alternate-provider search inventory. The only full text supplied is ar5iv and is corrupted at equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1. Retain only the legible Lemma 2.5/Theorems 4.4–4.5 linkage; do not reconstruct missing formulas.

## Gaps
No non-ar5iv native arXiv, publisher, or other-provider full-text excerpt, digest, and stable locators were supplied. Thus the complete verbatim equations (8)–(10) and all valid-tuple inequalities remain unavailable. “Valid \(\varphi\)” is a theorem hypothesis, but its complete conditions cannot be classified; the two \(N\)-inequalities are legible proof-only branches. The requested certificate is not established.

## Next
Obtain an uncorrupted bounded excerpt from a non-ar5iv provider containing Definition 2.1, equations (8)–(10), Lemma 2.5, and Theorems 4.4–4.5, with provider URL, digest, and stable locators.
